newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. aircraft carrier leaks oil at its Japan port.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aircraft carrier leaks oil at its Japan port.

text.p: Japanese patrol boats and U.S. Navy ships were mobilised on Saturday after an estimated 35,000 litres of oil spilled from the U.S. aircraft carrier Independence at its home port of Yokosuka, Japan's Maritime Safety Agency said.

The spill, equivalent to about 200 drums of oil, occurred after midnight and had not spread outside waters around the U.S. Navy's Yokosuka base, headquarters of the U.S. 7th Fleet, 45 km (28 miles) southwest of Tokyo, authorities said.
The oil was spilled when crew members attempting to adjust the ship's flotation level discharged fuel instead of bilge water, a U.S. naval official said.

Eight Japanese patrol boats and U.S. Navy ships set up oil fences to contain the spill and poured water on the slick to help it evaporate and protect the nearby Tokyo Bay, whose fisheries suffered a serious oil spill one month earlier.
The 80,643-tonne Independence has been based at Yokosuka since 1991 and is slated to be decommissioned and replaced by the carrier Kitty Hawk next year.
